trophies.guide: This is the trophy that ends the hunt: it pops the moment the other 54 are all earned, so there is no separate task to do for it. Work through the roadmap in this guide instead — story first, then the stranger strands, the activities and the collectibles, and finally the 100% completion checklist. Every trophy is single-player and offline, so no online mode or second playthrough is needed. PowerPyx rates the whole set 4 out of 10 in difficulty and estimates about 200 hours to the platinum, which makes this a long grind rather than a hard one. Keep cheats off for the whole run, since guides report that cheats disable trophies and saving. Track your count on the checklist page of this guide.

trophies.guide: This is the first story trophy most players will earn, and it cannot be missed. Play the opening mission Gone Fishing in Chapter 1, which introduces fishing with Cal and the basic controls of the game. Follow the on-screen prompts through the mission from start to finish — there is no special requirement, no time limit and no optional objective to worry about. The trophy pops as soon as the mission ends and the results screen clears. Because it is tied to a mandatory story mission, you cannot skip it or fail it permanently; if a mission attempt goes wrong, simply retry it and finish it. Treat it as your first checklist tick and move on to the rest of Chapter 1.

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 1 and this trophy unlocks when the chapter closes. Chapter trophies are automatic story rewards, so there is nothing extra to collect and nothing to look up — just keep playing the golden mission markers until the chapter ends. Before you leave Chapter 1, do one thing the guides all warn about: the first meditation at Jason's house, which Lucia offers after the mission Down to Earth. PowerPyx and GTABase both flag it as the only interaction in the game that may be missable, and it counts toward Positive Mental Attitude. Do it, then make a manual save at the start of Chapter 2 so you always have a way back.

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 2 and this trophy unlocks when the chapter closes. Like the other chapter trophies it is automatic and cannot be missed, so the only job is to keep following the story missions until the chapter ends. Chapter 2 is also where the world opens up properly, with both Jason and Lucia playable and most of the side content becoming available, so use the gaps between story missions to try activities, meet strangers and start the collectible hunts. Several trophies need Jason and Lucia together, and those only become possible from this chapter onward. Keep a manual save at the start of each new chapter, since the game has no mission replay and a save is your only way back.

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 3 and this trophy unlocks when the chapter closes. It is an automatic story reward with no extra requirement, so keep playing the main missions and it will come to you. By this point in the story you should have a good stock of side content open: stranger strands, races, shooting ranges and collectibles scattered across Leonida. It is worth clearing some of that between story missions rather than leaving everything for after the credits, because the variety breaks up the long story and several activity trophies feed directly into the 100% completion checklist. Make a manual save as Chapter 4 begins, as you have for every chapter so far.

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 4 and this trophy unlocks when the chapter closes. It is the last chapter trophy before the finale, and like the others it is automatic — complete the story missions and it pops. Before you push into the final mission, take a moment to tidy up: check this guide's checklist for any story-adjacent trophies you have not yet earned, and make a manual save before the final mission. Guides note that the game has no mission replay, so a save made here is your safety net for anything tied to the ending stretch. After the credits roll the open world stays available, so anything you have not finished can still be done in free roam.

trophies.guide: Complete the final story mission and this gold trophy is yours. It is the story's natural end point, so there is no trick to it: play the last mission through to its conclusion and the trophy pops with the credits. Make a manual save before you start the final mission, because the game has no mission replay and that save is the only way to revisit the ending stretch. The official description is the whole requirement — finish the final mission — so go by the official description rather than any rumoured extra condition. Once it pops, the open world remains available in free roam, which is where the bulk of the platinum hunt happens: the 100% checklist, the collectibles and the long activity grinds.

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run and this trophy unlocks at the mission's end. Mission trophies like this one are automatic: finish the mission and the trophy is yours, with no extra objective, no medal requirement and no time limit to beat. If you fail the mission partway through, retry it from the checkpoint or the mission start and finish it — a failed attempt never locks anything out. These named-mission trophies are the story's breadcrumbs, marking your progress through the chapters, so tick them off in this guide as you play and you will always know which missions you have left. Nothing about this trophy can be missed.

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist and this trophy unlocks when the mission ends. It is an automatic story reward, so the requirement is exactly what the official description says: finish the mission. Play it through, follow the mission objectives, and if anything goes wrong during the heist, retry from the checkpoint and finish it. Heist missions tend to be long and multi-stage, so take your time, use cover, and keep an eye on your health and ammo rather than rushing. There is no missable element here and no extra condition beyond completing the mission, so this trophy is simply a matter of reaching this point in the story and playing it out.

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play and this trophy unlocks at the mission's end. Like every named-mission trophy, it is automatic and unmissable: the official description is the full requirement, so finish the mission and the trophy pops. There is no medal system and no mission replay in this game, which means there is no pressure to play a mission perfectly — completion is all that counts. If you fail partway, retry and finish it. These mission trophies arrive steadily as you play the story, so by the time the credits roll you will have collected all of them without any special effort beyond finishing the campaign.

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners and this trophy unlocks when the mission ends. It is an automatic story reward with no hidden condition: the official description says to complete the mission, and that is everything. Play through the mission, follow its objectives, and retry from a checkpoint if you fail — nothing is lost by failing a story mission. Mission trophies like this one are the game's way of marking story progress, and they cannot be missed because the missions themselves are mandatory. Tick it off in this guide when it pops and keep moving through the story; the missable watch-list in this guide is the only thing that needs special attention.

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown and this trophy unlocks at the mission's end. VCIA is the game's airport, so expect this mission to involve aircraft and the airfield, but the trophy itself asks for nothing beyond finishing the mission. It is automatic and unmissable: play the mission through, retry from a checkpoint if you fail, and the trophy pops when the mission completes. Story missions never need to be replayed for a better result, since there are no gold medals and no mission replay feature. Finish the mission, tick the trophy off in this guide, and carry on with the story — the airport area is also worth remembering for the Catch Me If You Can trophy later.

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory and this trophy unlocks when the mission ends. It is an automatic story reward, exactly as the official description states — finish the mission and the trophy is yours. Military-flavoured missions like this one can be heavy on combat, so stock up on ammo and armour before you start, use cover, and retry from checkpoints if a section goes wrong. There is no extra condition, no medal and nothing to collect during the mission for this trophy. Once it pops, you are near the end of the story's mission list, so make sure your manual save before the final mission is in place.

trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the in-game completion checklist, which you can find under Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion. This is the hardest trophy in the set according to PowerPyx, but the requirements are lenient: PowerPyx reports it is closer to 60% of true completion, with most side quests not required and collectibles only partly required. The checklist asks for things like 300 of the 397 stunts, scanning 200 of 277 base model vehicles, studying 100 of 255 animals through binoculars, and 70 of the 80 challenges. Most of that progress comes naturally from the other trophies, so work the rest of this guide first and treat this as the final tidy-up. Nothing on the checklist is missable.

trophies.guide: Complete any 250 of the 397 stunts scattered across Leonida, and this silver trophy pops. PowerPyx breaks the stunts into four kinds: 130 stunt jumps over ramps, 202 flights under bridges, 40 knife flights between buildings, and 25 base jumps with a parachute. You do not need all 397 — 250 is enough for the trophy — but the 100% completion checklist asks for 300, so keep going past this trophy if you are chasing the platinum. Stunts are best done in free roam after the story, when you can pick them off with fast bikes, planes and helicopters at your own pace. Your progress is tracked in the game, so work through them steadily rather than in one sitting.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity in the game at least once. PowerPyx notes that the game's tracker counts 9 types of activities, so the job is simply to sample each one: races, fishing, the shooting range, arcade games, bowling, drone races and the other activities Leonida offers. You do not need to win, finish first or earn a medal — trying is enough, which makes this one of the easiest trophies on the list. It is a good early trophy to chase because it forces you to tour the activities and find the ones you enjoy, and several of them have their own trophies waiting behind them. If one activity type seems hard to find, check the map icons and the activities menu in the game.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge. PowerPyx reports there are 42 challenges across 12 shooting range locations, so this is a long accuracy grind rather than a single visit. Each range offers several challenges with different weapons and targets, and gold means hitting the top score band, not just passing. Visit the ranges as you unlock them, learn each challenge's target pattern, and take your time — rushing shots is what costs you the gold. Use the weapon the challenge gives you, aim for the high-value targets first, and replay any challenge that lands silver or bronze until it turns gold. Nothing here is missable, so you can return to any range in free roam.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of its locations around Leonida. Drone races are one of the game's activities: find the Top Fun markers on the map, enter a race, and fly the drone through the course faster than your rivals. The trophy needs a win at every location, not just one, so you will have to visit them all. Learn each course's turns before you race it flat out, cut corners only where the gates allow, and keep the drone steady rather than overcorrecting. If a location keeps beating you, retry it — there is no limit on attempts and nothing here is missable. Winning everywhere also counts toward your activity progress for the 100% checklist.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races across Leonida. The key word is different: winning the same race twenty times will not do it, so you need to work through the race list and take first place in twenty distinct events. Races cover cars, bikes, boats and more, and each has its own route and vehicle class, so vary your approach and pick the right vehicle for each course. Learn a route with a practice run before you race it for real, brake early for tight corners, and use slipstreaming on the straights. Nothing here is missable — every race stays available in free roam after the story — so chip away at the list between other activities and the count will build up.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the fishing contact you meet in the opening mission Gone Fishing, and fishing challenges against him are the way to settle who is the better angler. Head to a fishing spot, start a challenge with Cal, and out-fish him by landing more or bigger catches within the challenge's rules — watch the line tension, reel steadily, and do not let the fish snap the line. If you lose, challenge him again; there is no penalty for losing and no limit on attempts. Do this in Chapter 1 as well as later, since fishing is available from the start of the game, and a win here is one of the early activity trophies you can bank before the story moves on.

trophies.guide: Find an arcade machine in Leonida and complete one full game on it. Arcade machines are scattered around bars, clubs and arcades, so look for the glowing cabinets and interact with one to start playing. You only need to complete a game, not beat a high score or finish every machine, so pick a game that suits you and play it through to the end. If the game you pick is hard, try another cabinet — any completed arcade game counts. This is a quick, easy trophy to grab early, and it also counts as one of the activity types for Master of None, so it does double duty on your checklist. Nothing about it is missable.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's stranger mission strand. Stranger missions are side content offered by characters you meet around Leonida, marked on the map when they have work for you. Follow Andy's strand from its first mission through to its last, completing each job as it appears, and this trophy pops when the final one ends. Stranger strands unlock gradually as you explore, so if Andy has nothing for you yet, keep playing the story and check back — new missions appear as the game progresses. There are several of these final-mission trophies, one per stranger, and completing eight strands in total also earns Strangers & Freaks, so they are worth doing as a set.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's stranger mission strand. Like the other stranger finales, this one is the last job in a chain: meet Kenton, work through each mission he offers in order, and the trophy unlocks when the final mission ends. Stranger strands appear over the course of the game, so do not worry if Kenton's missions are not all available at once — play the story, explore Leonida, and return to his marker whenever it shows up. Nothing in a stranger strand is missable, and everything stays available in free roam after the credits, so you can finish Kenton's chain at your own pace. It also counts toward the eight strands needed for Strangers & Freaks.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's stranger mission strand. Work through Billy's missions in order, from the first meeting to the last job, and this trophy pops when the final mission ends. Stranger missions are optional side content, so they never block the story and never expire — if Billy's marker is not showing, keep playing and exploring, and it will appear as the game opens up more of Leonida. Each stranger's strand is short, usually a handful of missions, so they are a good change of pace between story chapters. Finishing Billy's strand also moves you one step closer to Strangers & Freaks, which needs eight completed strands across the state.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight full stranger mission strands across Leonida. Strangers are side characters with their own short mission chains, marked on the map when they have work — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have one, and there are more besides. Pick a stranger, finish every mission in their chain, and that strand counts; do that eight times and this silver trophy pops. The strands unlock as you progress through the story and explore, so do not expect all eight to be available in Chapter 1. They are all optional, none is missable, and all stay open in free roam after the story, so you can finish them in any order and at any pace you like.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's stranger mission strand. Follow Randy's chain from its first mission to its last, completing each job in order, and the trophy unlocks when the final mission ends. Stranger strands are spread across Leonida and open up as the story progresses, so if Randy's missions seem to stall, play more of the main story and check his marker again later. Nothing in these strands is missable and they all remain available after the credits, so there is no rush and no risk of locking yourself out. Each finished strand also counts toward Strangers & Freaks, so Randy's finale is one of the eight you need for that silver trophy.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's stranger mission strand. Work through Tyrone's missions in order until the chain ends, and this trophy pops with the final mission's completion. Like the other stranger finales it is a straightforward finish-the-chain trophy: no special condition, no medal, nothing to collect during the missions. If Tyrone's marker is not on the map yet, keep playing the story and exploring — stranger strands appear gradually. All of them stay open in free roam after the story ends, so you can finish Tyrone whenever it suits you, and it counts as one of the eight strands for the Strangers & Freaks silver trophy.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida — this is the one trophy the guides flag as possibly missable, so read this carefully. Beebom reports 18 meditation spots in total, and all 18 are needed for the trophy, while only 15 count toward 100% completion. The first spot is the danger: after the Chapter 1 mission Down to Earth, Lucia suggests meditating at Jason's house, and that balcony session disappears once Chapter 1 ends, with no mission replay to go back. Do it before leaving Chapter 1. The other spots are marked with purple icons when you are close, and you can meditate at each with both Jason and Lucia. Keep a Chapter 1 manual save until this trophy pops.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt down a unique animal for Bret. Bret is a stranger contact tied to hunting, and the trophy asks for a specific, one-of-a-kind animal rather than any animal you happen across. Explore Leonida's wild areas — swamps, forests and countryside — and look for the hunting markers and clues that point to the unique animal's territory. Bring a rifle with a scope, move slowly, and watch the wind and your noise, since spooking the animal can send it running. Study animals through binoculars first if you can: PowerPyx notes that studying 100 of the 255 animals counts toward 100% completion, so hunting and studying go together. The trophy pops once the unique animal is taken for Bret.

trophies.guide: Complete three full collectible card sets. Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida, and a set is complete only when you hold every card in it — one missing card means the set does not count. Search systematically rather than at random: work county by county, check the usual hiding places like shops, bars, garages and roadside stops, and use the in-game progress tracking to see which cards you still need. Cards are a classic GTA collectible grind, so expect this to take several sessions of free-roam hunting after the story. Nothing about the cards is missable, so you can collect them in any order and finish the sets whenever you like. Three completed sets earn this silver trophy.

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It feature at 100 different locations across Leonida. WAiNK It is the game's photo-sharing style interaction: find a spot, open the WAiNK It prompt, and take the shot. The trophy needs 100 distinct locations, so repeating the same spot will not move the count — you have to travel. Fold this into your exploration: every time you visit a new town, landmark, beach or viewpoint, WAiNK It there before you leave. It pairs naturally with The Goodtime State, which asks you to explore all of Leonida, so do them together and the two counts will rise side by side. None of the locations is missable, so this is a steady free-roam grind.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's challenges. Challenges are the small goals tracked in the Progress menu — things like stunts, races, hunting, exploration and activity milestones — and there are 80 in total, so you need fifty of them. The good news is that most challenges overlap with other trophies: racing, stunts, meditating, collecting and exploring all feed the challenge list, so a large chunk of the fifty will complete themselves while you chase the rest of the guide. Open the Progress menu regularly to see which challenges are close to done and finish those first. PowerPyx notes the 100% checklist asks for 70 of the 80, so push past fifty if you are going for the platinum.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Build a four-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose the police and escape. You need Jason and Lucia together for this one, so wait until both are playable and your partner is following you. Cause enough trouble to reach four stars — the wanted level is shown on screen — then break line of sight, get out of the search area, and stay hidden until the stars clear. Use alleys, tunnels and the countryside to break the chase, swap vehicles if yours is too hot, and avoid running straight into roadblocks. The trophy pops once the wanted level is gone and you have escaped. If the police catch you, just try again.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner, keeping your wanted level alive the whole time. The trick is the chain: rob the first shop, leave with the police after you, and hit the second and third shops before the wanted level clears — if it drops to zero, the chain breaks and you start over. Plan a route with three shops close together, keep a fast getaway car parked outside each one, and have your partner with you from the start. Rob quickly, grab the cash, get out fast, and do not stop to fight the police between shops. Three shops in one continuous wanted run earns the trophy, so rehearse the route before you commit to it.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles across Leonida. Discovering a vehicle means encountering it in the world — driving past it, sitting in it, or otherwise registering it in your collection — so the count grows simply by exploring and using the variety of traffic around you. Cities are best for common cars, while the countryside, airfields and docks hide the rarer ones: boats, planes, trucks and off-road vehicles. PowerPyx notes that the 100% checklist asks you to scan 200 of the 277 base model vehicles, so this trophy is an early milestone on a longer vehicle hunt. Keep exploring new areas and the discoveries will come naturally.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Defeat five enemies during one single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-motion aiming mode, and the window it gives you is short, so you need five targets lined up and ready before you trigger it. Pick a fight with a group of enemies in the open, let them cluster, then activate Combat Focus and take them down one by one before the effect ends. Use a fast-firing weapon, aim for the head where you can, and do not waste the window on reloading or repositioning. If you only manage three or four, the count resets, so set the scene first and then commit. A busy gang shootout is the natural place to try it.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies
PowerPyx — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from VCIA, the game's airport. In plain terms: get yourself into an aircraft at the airport and take off without going through any proper channel — steal a plane from the runway or the hangars and get airborne. Expect the airport to be guarded and your wanted level to rise, so plan your approach: enter the airfield in a fast vehicle, grab the nearest plane, and get off the ground before security closes in. The trophy pops once you are airborne and away. It is a fun, low-stakes trophy with no missable element, so try it whenever you are near the airport with a plane in sight.

trophies.guide: Get into a Rhino tank — the official description is a joke about how hot it is inside one, but the job is simple: find a military tank and drive it. Tanks are guarded at military sites and appear when the wanted level gets very high, so expect a fight to reach one. A video guide on this trophy shows stealing a tank drawing a three-star wanted level, so bring armour, a fast approach vehicle, and a plan to get out of the base alive. Once you are in the driver's seat, the trophy should pop — drive it away, enjoy the firepower, and lose the wanted level at your leisure. Nothing about this trophy is missable.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. This is a stealth job, not a smash-and-grab: getting spotted is what fails it, so plan the robbery like a quiet break-in. Scout the store first, learn where the staff and cameras are, and move when the coast is clear — at night, with few people around, is the best time to try. Wear a mask if the game offers one, keep your weapon out of sight until the moment you need it, and get in and out without raising the alarm. If you are spotted, leave and try again later; a failed attempt costs nothing but time. Patience and timing matter more than firepower here.

trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape after each one. Bank vaults are the big robbery targets of the game, bigger and better guarded than shops or armored trucks, so each one needs planning: scout the bank, know your entry and exit, and have a fast getaway vehicle ready. Crack the vault, grab the cash, and get clear of the police before the wanted level ends you — escaping is part of the requirement, so the trophy only counts vaults you get away from. Do all five across the game at your own pace; the count is cumulative and nothing is missable. Five clean escapes earn this silver trophy and a healthy pile of cash.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape with the cash. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida, so watch for them on the roads — they are the slow, heavy, guarded vans, not ordinary traffic. Stop the truck, deal with its guards, crack it open and take the money, then get away before the police arrive in force. A fast getaway car parked nearby makes the escape much easier, and a quiet road is a better ambush spot than a busy intersection. The escape matters: the trophy needs you to get away clean after the robbery, not just to open the truck. Once you are clear and the wanted level fades, the trophy pops.

trophies.guide: Explore every part of Leonida — the whole state, from Vice City to the swamps, the beaches, the farmland and the small towns. The trophy tracks map discovery, so the job is to visit every region and uncover the map until nothing is left unexplored. Drive the highways, take the back roads, and check the map regularly for dark, unvisited patches. It pairs naturally with the collectible hunts: WAiNK It spots, meditation spots, cards and vehicles are all scattered across the same map, so explore with a purpose and several counts will rise together. Nothing is missable here, and the trophy pops as soon as the last corner of the state is revealed.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang in Leonida. Gangs run their own off-the-books businesses — drug labs, chop shops, smuggling dens and the like — and the trophy asks you to hit one operation for every gang, not just your favourite target. Learn which gangs hold which territory, find their operations on the map or through exploration, and rob each one in turn. Expect armed resistance at every site, so go in prepared and have a getaway ready. The count is per gang, so keep a note of which gangs you have already hit and which are left. Nothing here is missable, and the operations stay available in free roam after the story.

Go by the official description here, because the exact unlock method for this trophy is not yet confirmed: PowerPyx lists it among the trophies whose method is not yet known, and other launch guides say the same. The sensible approach is to head to Ocean Beach, find a beachfront bar or club with a view over the water, and order a cocktail there — the kind of relaxed, location-based moment the description suggests. Try it at sunset or in the evening, when beach bars are at their liveliest, and if it does not pop, try other beachfront venues. Do not trust any specific step that cites no source; check the cited guides as they update.

Pick a showroom, get a fast car inside or steal the display car, and floor it through the window. If it does not pop on the first try, try another showroom or another angle. trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and follow through on your throw. Head to the alley, rent a lane, and play a game of bowling — the trophy's name is about the follow-through of a bowl, so the requirement is to play properly rather than just walk in and out. Pick up a ball, aim down the lane, and release with a smooth follow-through; completing a game or a good run of frames at this specific alley is what counts. The alley is named in the official description, so make sure you are at Kolt & Associates and not another bowling spot. It is a relaxed, easy trophy, and it also counts as an activity type toward Master of None.

trophies.guide: Make choices — for better or worse — and live with them. Go by the official description, because the exact trigger for this trophy is not yet confirmed by the cited guides. Play the story naturally, make the choices that come up, and the trophy should pop when a meaningful choice is resolved. Do not chase a specific rumoured decision that cites no source; keep a manual save before big story choices so you can revisit them, and check the cited guides as they confirm the trigger.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a melee drive-by. The trophy's method is still being confirmed by the guides, so go by the official description and treat the details as unconfirmed. The idea is simple enough: get a vehicle moving, get close to a target on foot, and strike them with a melee weapon from the vehicle instead of shooting. A slow drive-by past a pedestrian, with a bat or similar weapon ready, is the obvious way to try it. Pick a quiet street so you are not fighting the police at the same time, line the vehicle up alongside the target, and swing as you pass. Check the cited guides for a confirmed method as they update.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty money you pick up from robberies and heists, and they cannot be spent as they are — they have to be cleaned through contacts who take a cut. Find your laundering contacts, hand over the marked bills, and bank the clean cash; the trophy counts your total laundered earnings, so keep at it until the $250,000 mark is reached. Robberies are the best source of marked bills, so this trophy pairs naturally with Maximum Withdrawal, A Classic Blitz Play and Retail Therapy. It is a cumulative total, not one single haul, and nothing about it is missable.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops in Leonida. This is a cumulative total, so every dollar you spend in any shop counts — clothes, weapons, food, car parts, ammunition, anything with a price tag. The fastest way is to buy the expensive things you actually want: a good wardrobe, weapon upgrades, vehicle modifications and property-related purchases all add up quickly. Do not waste money on things you will never use just to hit the number; play normally, buy what you need, and check your spending total in the game from time to time. By the late game, after the big story payouts and the robbery income, $100,000 of spending will have taken care of itself.

trophies.guide: Buy every garage property in Leonida. Garage properties are the places where you store your vehicle collection, and each one costs money — so this trophy is really a money trophy in disguise. Save up through the story missions, robberies and laundering, then buy the garages one by one as you can afford them. Check the property listings on the in-game map or phone to see which garages are still unowned, and buy them in whatever order suits your cash flow. Owning all of them also gives you somewhere to keep the vehicles you discover for Whip It Good and register for On the Spot, so it supports the rest of the cleanup nicely.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the game's vehicle service app on your in-game phone, and registering a vehicle means adding it to the app — likely by owning the vehicle and entering it through the app, so that it is logged under your name. Collect ten vehicles you like, from cars to bikes, and register each one through the app until the count hits ten. The vehicles you discover for Whip It Good and store in the garages you buy for Little Boxes are the natural candidates, so do this trophy alongside those two. It is a small, easy trophy with nothing missable about it, and it pops as soon as the tenth registration goes through.
